title: HigherSmoothBilevel.lean

problem_class.label: strongly_convex
problem_class.details: Only the lower-level function g(x,·) is required to be μ-strongly convex for every x.

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: The unconstrained hyper-objective Φ(x)=f(x,argmin_y g(x,y)) may be nonconvex.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: Each query (x,y) returns the exact full derivatives of both f and g; replies have no noise or history dependence. Higher derivatives are not supplied.

oracle.label: function_value
oracle.details: The same query also returns both exact function values f(x,y) and g(x,y).

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: X and Y are finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Globally, f is C² with bounded derivative ‖Df‖≤L and L-Lipschitz first and second derivatives; g is C³ with L-Lipschitz first, second, and third derivatives. Public parameters satisfy 0<μ≤L, Δ>0, G≥0, ε>0. Initialization satisfies Φ(x0)−inf Φ≤Δ and ‖∇_y g(x0,y0)‖≤G. All Params are public; f and g are hidden instance functions.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/HigherSmoothBilevel.lean: Params; Instance; spec.Public; spec.publicInput; spec.valid; spec.admissible.

accuracy.label: gradient_norm
accuracy.details: Output x∈X must be a differentiability point of Φ and satisfy ‖∇Φ(x)‖≤ε, without squaring the norm.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: The output criterion holds almost surely over the joint algorithm and oracle seed law, within the supplied fixed oracle budget.

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: An established unconstrained nonconvex–strongly-convex bilevel formulation with exact first-order access and higher-order smoothness assumptions for accelerated stationarity guarantees.

descriptionHtml:
Higher-Order Smooth Bilevel Optimization

We consider minimizing F(x)=f(x,y⋆(x)) over a finite-dimensional real inner product space X, where y⋆(x) minimizes g(x,⋅) over another such space Y. The functions f,g:X×Y→R are respectively twice and three times continuously differentiable, with bounded first derivative of f, Lipschitz derivatives through these orders, and uniform strong convexity of the lower problem. Given initial points have bounded outer objective gap and lower gradient residual. The oracle returns both function values and first derivatives. For ε>0, the goal is an output x¯ where F is differentiable and ∥∇F(x¯)∥≤ε almost surely under P, the law of the algorithm’s randomness.

Write y⋆(x)=argminy∈Yg(x,y),F(x)=f(x,y⋆(x)). The lower minimizer exists and is unique by the assumptions below. The bilevel problem is minx∈XF(x). On X and Y, norms are induced by their inner products. On Z=X×Y, we use the product norm ∥(x,y)∥Z=max{∥x∥,∥y∥}. For a scalar function h on Z, write dh for its first derivative and ∇2h, ∇3h for its second and third derivatives, viewed as bilinear and trilinear forms on Z. Their norms ∥⋅∥op are the induced operator norms for this product norm. Gradients on X and Y use the respective inner products.

The algorithm receives X, Y, initial points x0∈X, y0∈Y, and all parameters L,μ,Δ,G,ε, whose ranges are 0<μ≤L,Δ>0,G≥0,ε>0.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Higher-order regularity). The functions satisfy f∈C2(Z;R) and g∈C3(Z;R). For every z,w∈Z, ∥df(z)∥op≤L,∥df(z)−df(w)∥op≤L∥z−w∥Z,∥∇2f(z)−∇2f(w)∥op≤L∥z−w∥Z,∥dg(z)−dg(w)∥op≤L∥z−w∥Z,∥∇2g(z)−∇2g(w)∥op≤L∥z−w∥Z,∥∇3g(z)−∇3g(w)∥op≤L∥z−w∥Z.

Assumption 2 (Lower-level strong convexity). For every x∈X and y,v∈Y, g(x,v)≥g(x,y)+⟨∇yg(x,y),v−y⟩+μ2∥v−y∥2.

Assumption 3 (Initial bounds). The given initial points satisfy F(x0)−F(x)≤Δfor every x∈X,∥∇yg(x0,y0)∥≤G.

Queries may be made at any z∈Z. A single oracle call returns the exact tuple (f(z),g(z),df(z),dg(z)). After the allotted oracle calls, the output x¯∈X must satisfy F is differentiable at x¯,∥∇F(x¯)∥≤εP-a.s.

comparisonHtml:
Finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces X,Y; f∈C2, g∈C3, ∥Df∥≤L, and Df,D2f,Dg,D2g,D3g are L-Lipschitz (max product norm). Each g(x,⋅) is μ-strongly convex, 0<μ≤L, F(x0)−infF≤Δ>0, and ∥∇yg(x0,y0)∥≤G. Exact joint (f,g,Df,Dg) queries are available. Target: ∥∇F(x^)∥≤ε, ε>0; (1) succeeds for every seed.

Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations

(2) AccF2BA+ (Chen, Ji, et al. 2026), Thm. F.2 O(ΔL3/4κ13/4ε−7/4χ6P) first-order calls; ερF≤LF. (1): κ smaller leading cost when ΔLκ4/ε3≥1, up to logs; deterministic, dimension-free FOSP instead of probability 1−δ. (1) loses SOSP. With heterogeneous constants, gain requires L¯1/4μ1/2<L11/2L21/4.
(3) AccF2BA (Chen, Ma, et al. 2026), Thm. 5.2 O(ΔL3/4κ15/4ε−7/4χ6P) first-order calls; additionally f∈C3. (1): κ smaller leading cost when ΔLκ4/ε3≥1, up to logs; every-seed FOSP without dimension/confidence logs. (1) loses the probability-1−δ SOSP guarantee.
(4) RAHGD (Yang et al. 2023), Cor. 3.6 O(ΔL3/4κ13/4ε−7/4P) total gradient, Jacobian-vector and Hessian-vector calls. (1): κ smaller leading total cost when ΔLκ4/ε3≥1, up to logs; only first-order queries.
(5) Derived bound: FSBA/LFSBA (Yang et al. 2026), Thms. 3.4, 4.3; finite-difference Hessians O([κ+D+ΔL(κ3+Dκ11/4)ε−3/2]P) first-order calls. (1) is dimension-free; leading cost improves up to logs when ε≳L/(κ1/4+D)4 and startup is dominated. (1) loses SOSP; worse accuracy exponent (7/4 versus 3/2), losing at fixed dimension for sufficiently small ε.

Abbr: F(x)=f(x,arg⁡minyg(x,y)); κ=L/μ; D=dim⁡X+dim⁡Y; dx=dim⁡X; ℓ=1+log⁡[κ(1+L/ε)(1+Δ/ε)(1+G/ε)]; χ=1+log+⁡(dx/(δε)), log+⁡t=max{0,log⁡t}, 0<δ<1. P denotes the cited bounds’ additional polylogarithmic factors in smoothness, conditioning, accuracy and initialization (and confidence for (2), (3)). FOSP: first-order stationarity; SOSP additionally bounds λmin(∇2F). LF,ρF are the gradient and Hessian Lipschitz bounds for F. L1,L2 are separate derivative Lipschitz bounds, L¯=maxqLq.

import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Calculus
import LongTails.Template
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.ContDiff.Defs
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.MeanValue
import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Module.FiniteDimension

set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

namespace LongTails.Setups.HigherSmoothBilevel

open OracleTemplate MeasureTheory

structure Params where
  X : Type
  [normedX : NormedAddCommGroup X]
  [innerX : InnerProductSpace ℝ X]
  [finiteX : FiniteDimensional ℝ X]
  Y : Type
  [normedY : NormedAddCommGroup Y]
  [innerY : InnerProductSpace ℝ Y]
  [finiteY : FiniteDimensional ℝ Y]
  x0 : X
  y0 : Y
  L : ℝ
  μ : ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  G : ℝ
  ε : ℝ

attribute [instance] Params.normedX Params.innerX Params.finiteX
  Params.normedY Params.innerY Params.finiteY

structure Instance (p : Params) where
  f : p.X × p.Y → ℝ
  g : p.X × p.Y → ℝ

noncomputable def lowerSolution {p : Params} (I : Instance p) (x : p.X) : p.Y :=
by
  classical
  exact if h : ∃ y : p.Y, ∀ z, I.g (x, y) ≤ I.g (x, z) then Classical.choose h else 0

noncomputable def hyperObjective {p : Params} (I : Instance p) (x : p.X) : ℝ :=
  I.f (x, lowerSolution I x)

abbrev Reply (p : Params) :=
  ℝ × ℝ × ((p.X × p.Y) →L[ℝ] ℝ) × ((p.X × p.Y) →L[ℝ] ℝ)

noncomputable def firstOrderReply {p : Params} (I : Instance p) (z : p.X × p.Y) : Reply p :=
  (I.f z, I.g z, fderiv ℝ I.f z, fderiv ℝ I.g z)

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance := Instance
  Query p := p.X × p.Y
  Reply := Reply
  Output p := p.X
  publicInput p := p
  valid p := 0 < p.μ ∧ p.μ ≤ p.L ∧ 0 < p.Δ ∧ 0 ≤ p.G ∧ 0 < p.ε
  admissible p I O :=
    ContDiff ℝ 2 I.f ∧
    ContDiff ℝ 3 I.g ∧
    (∀ z, ‖fderiv ℝ I.f z‖ ≤ p.L) ∧
    (∀ z w, ‖fderiv ℝ I.f z - fderiv ℝ I.f w‖ ≤ p.L * ‖z - w‖) ∧
    (∀ z w, ‖fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ I.f) z - fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ I.f) w‖ ≤ p.L * ‖z - w‖) ∧
    (∀ z w, ‖fderiv ℝ I.g z - fderiv ℝ I.g w‖ ≤ p.L * ‖z - w‖) ∧
    (∀ z w, ‖fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ I.g) z - fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ I.g) w‖ ≤ p.L * ‖z - w‖) ∧
    (∀ z w, ‖fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ I.g)) z -
      fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ I.g)) w‖ ≤ p.L * ‖z - w‖) ∧
    (∀ x y z, I.g (x, y) + fderiv ℝ I.g (x, y) (0, z - y) +
      p.μ / 2 * ‖z - y‖ ^ 2 ≤ I.g (x, z)) ∧
    (∀ x, hyperObjective I p.x0 - hyperObjective I x ≤ p.Δ) ∧
    ‖gradient (fun y => I.g (p.x0, y)) p.y0‖ ≤ p.G ∧
    (∀ history z seed, O.answer history (0, z) seed = firstOrderReply I z)
  successful p I output P := ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : Measure _),
    DifferentiableAt ℝ (hyperObjective I) (output ω) ∧
      ‖gradient (hyperObjective I) (output ω)‖ ≤ p.ε

end LongTails.Setups.HigherSmoothBilevel
